pairs.title: Riemann solvers for hyperbolic systems
pairs.scope: For f in C3 on an open admissible set G in Rm, define strictly hyperbolic conservation systems and admissible-state set, characteristic families, Rankine–Hugoniot and Lax admissibility as definitions. Prove the local small-data Riemann solver near a state where each field is genuinely nonlinear or linearly degenerate, with clearly bounded neighborhood; do not promise arbitrary large-data solutions. Define Godunov, Roe and HLL fluxes. Prove consistency and conservation; Roe property is an algebraic identity, not entropy admissibility. For ideal-gas Euler define pressure mathematically on rho>0, E>|m|²/(2rho), derive eigenstructure and give admissibility/failure conditions; HLL wave-speed bounds are explicit hypotheses or separately proved bounds.
pairs.proof_route: Prove eigenpair smoothness under simple spectrum, local rarefaction integral curves, shock curves using an augmented Rankine–Hugoniot implicit-function argument, tangent matching and wave-composition invertibility; verify weak jumps. Prove HLL flux by integrating the two-wave approximate conservation balance. Derive Euler sound speed and contact eigenvector locally. An exact Riemann procedure uses a bracketed pressure root with finite iteration budget and vacuum detection; existence/uniqueness of that root is a separate lemma.
pairs.examples: acoustic system, Sod tube, contact, Roe expansion shock/vacuum failure.
pairs.missing_prerequisites: /smallest suppliers:** NA09 local inverse/implicit tools plus root ODE existence, existing scalar Riemann theorem for comparison only; locally author the system wave-curve lemmas.
pairs.source_locators: LeVeque, *Finite Volume Methods for Hyperbolic Problems* (2002), Chapters 11, 13–15; https://www.clawpack.org/riemann_book/ Euler and approximate-solvers chapters. Source reading outstanding.

Prove second-order smooth-region reconstruction where the limiter is inactive; prove scalar TVD for a stated flux/limiter/CFL update by Harten's incremental form. Prove WENO polynomial reproduction/consistency and optimal smooth-region order under explicit smoothness and weight asymptotics; near critical points state the actual JS order, not automatic fifth order. Include the scalar linear monotonicity/order barrier. Systems characteristic reconstruction is defined but receives no automatic scalar TVD theorem.
pairs.proof_route: Solve reconstruction moment equations; Taylor-expand candidate polynomials and smoothness indicators with uniform remainders; derive nonlinear weight asymptotics including epsilon scaling. Derive nonnegative incremental coefficients and sum their variation estimate. Give a concrete critical-point counterexample when hypotheses fail.

pairs.title: Positivity, invariant domains and entropy-stable systems fluxes
pairs.scope: Define convex invariant sets and convex entropy pairs for systems. Prove a first-order local Lax–Friedrichs/HLL invariant-domain update under a stated invariant Riemann-average hypothesis and CFL convex-combination coefficients; prove ideal-gas density/internal-energy positivity on the explicitly admitted wave-speed branch. Define entropy variables, two-point entropy-conservative flux and dissipative entropy-stable flux. Prove the semidiscrete cell entropy inequality from the exact Tadmor jump condition and positive semidefinite dissipation. Fully discrete entropy needs its own time-step theorem. Define a convex scaling positivity limiter and prove cell-average conservation plus positive quadrature-node states; do not claim cellwise pointwise positivity from finitely many nodes without a separate argument.
pairs.proof_route: Convexity of admissible Euler set; decompose updates into invariant Riemann averages. Multiply flux balances by entropy variables, telescope entropy potentials and bound dissipation. Limiter takes the maximal admissible scaling toward a positive mean; prove preservation and smooth-data accuracy only with a strict positive margin.
pairs.examples: near-vacuum Euler, entropy residual, conservative positivity rescaling, entropy-stable but insufficiently resolved shock.

pairs.title: Monotone Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman schemes and policy iteration
pairs.scope: Define monotone upwind and positive-interpolation semi-Lagrangian schemes for a specified first-order HJ/HJB Cauchy problem, and a discounted stationary Bellman equation on a periodic domain with compact or finite controls and bounded Lipschitz coefficients. Prove monotonicity, L∞ stability, consistency and numerical-scheme-to-viscosity convergence by a full half-relaxed-limit argument using the exact existing first-order comparison class. A control minimization over infinite controls is an explicit oracle or a finite control discretization with its own uniform Hamiltonian error. Define finite-control Howard/policy iteration for the assembled proper M-matrix Bellman system; prove monotone improvement and finite termination with deterministic tie handling/no switch on equal value, or state a separately proved contraction stopping bound. Include a concrete second-order Bellman controlled-diffusion scheme on a monotone diagonal-dominant/wide-stencil branch; prove its comparison/convergence with new second-order viscosity suppliers. No generic central stencil monotonicity for arbitrary anisotropic diffusion, no unproved universal convergence rate.
pairs.proof_route: Upwind/positive interpolation makes nodal update order preserving; positive discount gives stationary sup contraction and discrete comparison/unique solution. Finite policy matrices have verified M-matrix inverse positivity; compare successive value solutions, show each strict switch strictly improves at a component and eliminate repeated policies using tie rule, so finite policy space terminates. Derive consistency on smooth test functions including h²/dt interpolation and control-grid error where relevant. To pass numerical limits, choose strict touching test functions, extract near-maximal mesh nodes, apply discrete monotonicity replacing states by test-function values plus contact error, then take limsup/liminf; prove boundary/initial barriers and use continuous comparison to squeeze both limits. The published half-relaxed theorem applies to approximate PDE solutions, so this mesh-node consistency proof is genuinely new. For second order locally define semijets/degenerate ellipticity, prove the required theorem of sums via sup/inf convolution and twice-differentiability arguments (with actual local analytic suppliers), then doubling variables and discount produce comparison; prove Perron/barrier existence or obtain it from convergent discrete approximants. These large but established proofs belong here before their consumers, not a citation to Barles–Souganidis. Restrict a second-order theorem to the coefficient/boundary class for which all those estimates are supplied.
pairs.examples: eikonal/HJ kink, discounted control switching, monotone versus nonmonotone stencil, diagonal diffusion Bellman manufactured value, infinite-control quantization.
pairs.missing_prerequisites: /smallest suppliers:** NA23/25, PE31, existing first-order viscosity definitions/half-relaxed limits/comparison, canonical linear solves; local mesh touching lemma, discrete comparison/M-matrix, finite-policy monotonicity, control discretization, second-order semijet/theorem-of-sums/comparison/barriers. Choice assumptions follow actual extraction/projection proofs.
pairs.source_locators: Barles–Souganidis, *Convergence of approximation schemes for fully nonlinear second order equations*, Asymptotic Analysis 4 (1991), 271–283, https://doi.org/10.3233/ASY-1991-4305 (full proof must be locally supplied); Crandall–Ishii–Lions, *User's guide to viscosity solutions of second order partial differential equations*, Bull. AMS 27 (1992), 1–67, https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9207212, second-order theorem of sums/comparison; Falcone–Ferretti 2014, https://doi.org/10.1137/1.9781611973051, numerical HJB/policy chapters; Bokanowski–Maroso–Zidani, *Some convergence results for Howard's algorithm*, SIAM JNA 47 (2009), 3001–3026, https://doi.org/10.1137/08073041X, precise finite-policy and convergence hypotheses to verify.
